facts.fact: Seville is much more than its undeniable monumentality. It is a city that comes to life on the streets and in its large open spaces such as the enormous Plaza de España, the María Luisa Park or the avant-garde Setas de Sevilla. And for the most authentic Sevillian atmosphere, try going for tapas in the historic quarter in popular areas such as Alameda, Macarena, Nervión, Los Remedios or Triana. Marinated ‘pescaíto’ (fish), small filled rolls, typical snails, fino (white wine), manzanilla (sweet wine) or a cold beer are a must on any tapas outing.
